resolutions.researcher_notes: The only capacity figure found for the Gazli-Kagan corridor, in any language, is Sputnik Uzbekistan (2021-11-29, quoting the Ministry of Energy): 'po dannym ministerstva, za sutki cherez dannyy magistral'nyy gazoprovod prokhodit 35 mln kubometrov prirodnogo gaza' ('per the ministry, 35 million cubic meters of natural gas pass daily through this trunk gas pipeline') -- re-verified directly today. That sentence is stated in the context of describing the corridor's THREE existing lines together (I/II from 1973-1983 plus III from 2006), i.e. it reads as whole-corridor aggregate throughput as of late 2021, not a figure isolated to lines I & II -- and the same 35.00 is also recorded on sibling row P3984 (presumptively line III), which would double-count corridor capacity if both rows cite it as their own. No source anywhere breaks 35 mcm/day down per individual line. Searched (RU): 'Газли-Каган газопровод производительность млн кубометров сутки'; re-fetched the Sputnik article, the energybase.ru piece (blocked, IP-restricted on this fetch), and the tafsilar.info piece (returns an empty client-render stub, same as the prior audit found). Not staging a ref for a value I cannot confirm is correctly scoped to lines I/II specifically -- matches the prior deep-sweep audit's finding on this cell exactly.

No independent source gives a length for lines I/II specifically (115.30 km). Sources found give lengths for OTHER segments of the same corridor -- 140 km for the new 4th line (energybase.ru, Sputnik), and a separate 48 km (km0-10 + km78-116) reconstruction span turned up by the prior audit -- but nothing for the 1973/1983 lines this row covers. Re-verified today: re-fetched the Sputnik article (confirms only the 1973-1983/2006 commissioning years, no length figures at all for any line), attempted energybase.ru (IP-blocked on this fetch, consistent with a geo/anti-bot block, not a deletion) and tafsilar.info (empty client-render stub). Searched (RU): 'Газли-Каган газопровод 115 км диаметр 720 1020' (web search budget exhausted before results returned; relied on direct re-fetch of the seed_citations set instead, which is the country's documented productive vein). Genuine UNRESOLVED after a Russian-language search -- matches the prior deep-sweep audit's finding on this cell exactly.

No independent source confirms 720/1020 mm for lines I/II specifically. The prior audit found a 1020 mm figure tied to a 2005-2006 reconstruction of km 78-116 (48 km) -- plausibly line III territory (opened 2006), not lines I/II -- and did not use it here to avoid misattributing another line's spec to this row; I concur after re-checking the same lead. Re-fetched today: gazligs.com (Gazli underground-storage facility page) names the pipelines meeting at Gazli as Bukhara-Urals, Middle Asia-Center and Gazli-Chimkent, and states Uztransgaz operates the local 'Gazli LPU/UMG', but never names 'Gazli-Kagan' or gives any diameter figure -- fails the segment-specificity test the same way the prior audit found. Searched (RU) for a line-specific diameter via the seed citation set; none give one. Genuine UNRESOLVED after a Russian-language search -- matches the prior deep-sweep audit's finding on this cell exactly.

Re-verified the prior audit's circumstantial lead directly today: gazligs.com (fetched via https://www.gazligs.com/ -- the bare https://gazligs.com/ host fails TLS altname validation, host mismatch not a live/dead signal) describes АО «Узтрансгаз» as operating the local 'Газлийское УМГ' (Gazli gas-transport management unit) and lists the pipelines meeting at the Gazli storage hub as Bukhara-Urals, Middle Asia-Center and Gazli-Chimkent -- it does NOT name 'Gazli-Kagan' anywhere on the page, so it fails the segment-naming requirement (a page must name THIS pipeline, not an adjacent one at the same hub). utg.uz/ru/about/history/ remains a confirmed dead link per the country note; utg.uz/en/press-service/.../implementation-of-the-investment-program-is-undergo/ 404s outright on this fetch (differs from the seed citation's URL casing/path -- likely moved or retired, not evidence for or against operator attribution).
